2025-02-11

Slide 1: Introduction

Visualizations and Maps in R

  • Importance of clear, informative visualizations
  • Common mistakes to avoid
  • Overview of good and bad examples

Slide 2: Principles of Good Visualization

Key Elements:

  • Simplicity
  • Clarity
  • Relevance
  • Consistency

Slide 3: Good Example - Clear and Simple Plot

library(ggplot2)
data(mpg)
ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title="Engine Displacement vs. Highway Mileage")

  • Clear labels and title
  • Simple scatter plot

Slide 4: Bad Example - Overloaded Plot

ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=hwy, color=class, size=cty)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title="Overloaded Plot Example") +
  theme_minimal()

- Too much information in one plot - Hard to interpret

Slide 5: Choosing the Right Map for the Data

Map Types:

  • Choropleth maps
  • Scatter plots with coordinates
  • Heatmaps

Slide 6: Good Example - Choropleth Map

library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
world <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package="sf"))
## Reading layer `nc' from data source 
##   `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-x86_64/Resources/library/sf/shape/nc.shp' 
##   using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
## Simple feature collection with 100 features and 14 fields
## Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
## Dimension:     XY
## Bounding box:  xmin: -84.32385 ymin: 33.88199 xmax: -75.45698 ymax: 36.58965
## Geodetic CRS:  NAD27
ggplot(data = world) + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA)) +
  labs(title = "Area Distribution by Region")

- Clear regional differences - Proper use of color scales

Slide 7: Bad Example - Poor Map Color Choices

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = world) + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_b() +
  labs(title = "Bad Map Example")

- Color choice that doesn’t differentiate well for everyone (e.g., colorblindness)

Slide 8: Good Example - Using Facets in Maps

library(dplyr)
ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~class) +
  labs(title="Vehicle Class Facets")

- Facets make comparisons easy - Clearly segmented data

Slide 9: Bad Example - Overuse of Facets

ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~class + manufacturer) +
  labs(title="Overused Facets Example")

- Too many facets makes it hard to extract meaning - Can overwhelm the audience

Slide 10: Mapping with Interactive Visualizations

Using leaflet in R

library(leaflet)
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addMarkers(lng = -87.6298, lat = 41.8781, popup = "Chicago")
  • Interactive maps allow user exploration
  • Add custom markers and popups

Slide 11: Bad Example - Static Maps for Interactive Data

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(world, aes(fill = AREA)) + 
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title="Static Map for Interactive Data")

- Static map limits user interaction and exploration - Ineffective for interactive data

Slide 12: Conclusion

Best Practices:

  • Simplify your plots
  • Choose the right map type
  • Avoid visual clutter
  • Make interactive maps when appropriate

This provides a presentation structure with both good and bad examples, demonstrating clear principles of effective visualization and mapping in R. You can add images or further tweak the formatting for the final output in ioslides.
